originality.rationale: Full original 2026 Huygens path paper establishes the model, the all-length spectrum and the no-periodic-point Lyapunov interval, but does not claim the unique attracting branch immediately beyond the threshold, its square-root spatial profile or Floquet coefficient. Earlier authors’ small-coupling 3-clock work is restricted to diffeomorphism/attraction regimes, and a contemporaneous ring study treats different network geometry. Actual searches in published mathematical findings returned related period-two results for other systems, not the same K_N-sine path statement. This establishes best-evidence noncoverage, not exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: The cited new Huygens path theory identifies a sharp descent/stability boundary but does not describe actual dynamics just beyond it. The theorem resolves the concrete dynamical question by proving immediate birth of a locally unique attracting oscillation for every finite chain and an explicit alternating spatial shape and critical multiplier. The specific nonlinear coefficient distinguishes genuine supercritical birth from mere linear instability; this is more than an unmotivated parameter slice or routine normalization.
